caption: A phone lying face-up on a table in a dark room lights up, and its glow lights the objects around it from below.

sa.check: A phone lies on a table in a room.
Its glow lights the objects around it from below.

pc.expect: The objects are lit on the sides facing the screen and the glow changes when the screen's picture changes.
pc.fail: They are lit from above; or the glow is unchanged when the picture changes; or the far side of the room is lit.

pc.expect: The glow takes the screen's colour.
pc.fail: It is a different colour from the screen; or it is white with a coloured screen; or it changes colour with the screen steady.

pc.expect: The glow stops when the screen turns off.
pc.fail: The objects stay lit with the screen dark; or lit before it lights; or the glow moves with the phone still.

pc.expect: The glow is a soft spread from the screen.
pc.fail: It is a sharp beam; or it splits; or it is a geometric shape.

pc.expect: One phone and the objects around it.
pc.fail: A second phone appears; or an object vanishes; or the glow becomes solid.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The objects and the table stay the same.
pc.fail: An object changes colour rather than brightness; or moves; or the table changes.

note: Illumination: the on/off causality of electric lights belongs to Electricity; here only where the light goes once it exists is judged.
